Tables and SELECT results

Unit 2 · Week 4 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open a working copy of sql-starter.sqlite in a school-approved SQLite-capable application and locate its SQL editor. Alternatively execute sql-setup.sql once in a new empty database. Run one SELECT at a time. Use sql-workbook.md, sql-answers.md, sql-worked-queries.sql and sql-expected-results.json. The data are fictional. DueDate is valid YYYY-MM-DD TEXT and Returned is INTEGER 0/1 in this SQLite starter. Fixed reporting date: 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Tables and SELECT results

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Return to the earlier single-item Loan model. The reservation model was a separate normalisation exercise. This week uses SELECT queries to read data. Activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

2. The database we are using

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and prediction

Equipment stores EquipmentDescription. The starter is the earlier four-table Loan model, not the separate reservation register used in Week 3. Open the SQLite file as a database, not as a CSV import. Use the SQL editor, not a Python prompt. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

3. Parts of a query

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

SQL means Structured Query Language. A query asks the DBMS for a result. This week reads data with SELECT. Later chapters cover changes, joins and aggregates. A named-field SELECT returns requested columns without deleting other stored columns. Keywords are uppercase here for readability. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

4. A named-field query

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with predictions

Expect two columns and five rows. A comma separates the two field names. FROM names Equipment. ORDER BY makes the item-ID order explicit. The semicolon ends the statement. Compare the results with the stored table, which still has CategoryID. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

5. The complete query result

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

Five rows represent five physical items. E01 and E04 are different items with the same description. CategoryID remains in stored Equipment, even though it is absent from these selected columns. SELECT * requests every field, whereas naming fields makes the intended output clear. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

6. A first independent report

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook question 1. Expected query: SELECT BorrowerID, BorrowerLabel FROM Borrower ORDER BY BorrowerID; rows B001 Learner A, B002 Learner B, B003 Learner C, B004 Learner D. Keep requirement, SQL, prediction and actual result for self-review. Offer the Equipment model if needed, then ask for an independent explanation. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

7. A result is not a table edit

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

It remains stored. SELECT controls the returned columns, not the table definition. Learners can inspect Equipment again to verify all three columns remain. Do not confuse a query result with deleting fields or records. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

8. An asterisk to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

In this Equipment table, * includes EquipmentID, EquipmentDescription and CategoryID. The named-field example includes only the first two. Neither query changes the stored data. Naming columns states the intended output and avoids relying on every field in a changing schema. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.
